entry.title: What if we tried to eat the sun?

media:group.media:title: What if we tried to eat the sun?
media:group.media:description:
We’ve just refreshed the xkcd store! https://store.xkcd.com/
Get a copy of What If? 2 and Randall’s other books at: https://xkcd.com/books More serious answers to absurd questions at: https://what-if.xkcd.com/
This question comes from James, who asks: what percentage of the Sun's heat (per day) does the population of Earth eat in calories per year? What changes could be made to our diets for the amount of calories to equal the energy of the Sun?
Each year, humans eat about 0.000000000065% of the sun’s daily energy output. We’re going to need some help.

entry.title: If you put a toaster in a freezer, which wins?

media:group.media:title: If you put a toaster in a freezer, which wins?
media:group.media:description:
Get a copy of What If? 2 and Randall’s other books at: https://xkcd.com/books More serious answers to absurd questions at: https://what-if.xkcd.com/
I heard this question debated on a podcast I listen to, which asked: “Would a toaster still work in a freezer?” Here’s how they summed up the situation: You put a toaster in a freezer. You put some bread in there. You click it down. What even happens, right? Because if your answer is, "it would get hot," then the freezer hasn't done its job. But if you say "it would get cold," then the toaster hasn't done its job.
